prerequisites: B1 Spanish language certificate (required for international mobility students)
Mastery of knowledge from Calculus, Algebra and Geometry, Physics I, Physics II

learning_outcomes.text: Competence in critical contextualization of knowledge, establishing interrelationships with local and/or global social, economic, and environmental issues.
Competence in the sustainable use of resources and the prevention of negative impacts on the natural and social environment.
Competence in the application of ethical principles related to sustainability values in personal and professional conduct.
Competence in participating in community processes that promote sustainability.
Knowledge of the basic principles of fluid mechanics and their application to solving problems in the field of engineering. Calculation of pipes, channels, and fluid systems.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to solve problems.
Ability to make decisions.
Ability to organize and plan.
Ability to apply knowledge in practice.
Ability to work in a team.
Attitude of motivation for quality and continuous improvement.
Ability to analyze and synthesize.
Creativity and inventive spirit in solving scientific-technical problems.
Aptitude for oral and written communication in the native language.
Ability for autonomous and deep learning.
Ability to interpret technical documentation.
Ability for critical reasoning.
Ability to fluently use computers at a user level.
Theoretical and practical knowledge of the fundamentals that allow analyzing fluid motion and addressing problem-solving in engineering.

syllabus_topics: Fluidostatics: Introduction. Volume and surface forces. General fluidostatics equation. Hydrostatic force. Archimedes' principle.
Kinematics: Introduction. Trajectory, streamlines, pathlines, and streaklines. Substantial derivative. Integral theorems. Potential function and stream function.
General Equations: Continuity equation, momentum equation, and energy equation.
Flows with Dominant Viscosity: Introduction. Particular cases.
Dimensional Analysis and Physical Similarity: Theorems and applications.
